answer: The registry enforces Sybil resistance with a staked-verifier kernel: each new agent needs endorsement from an existing agent who posts collateral, and it enters a public attestation chain. A forge attempt, paying a verifier to mint fake siblings, burns that stake on dispute, and the required bond climbs geometrically with every identity a sponsor already vouched for. Coordinating a fable of fake operators thus costs more stake than those identities could earn back, while an honest agent pays one small deposit. Votes weight by bonded stake, so duplicates add nothing.
